science.title: Common misconceptions in life sciences about the concentrations and toxicity of perchlorates on Mars
science.description: Perchlorate is often portrayed as an obstacle to both the habitability and the human exploration of Mars, and therefore is the focus of extensive research in space life sciences. However, such research is being slowed down by misconceptions regarding (i) the concentrations microorganisms could be exposed to on Mars, whether naturally or in bioproduction systems, and (ii) the mechanisms behind its toxicity. This article highlights these misconceptions and proposes corrections.

science.title: Strain-driven and electric-field-tunable self-morphotropic phase boundary in nitride perovskite
science.description: Ultrahigh piezoelectricity has long been associated with chemically complex morphotropic phase boundaries (MPBs). However, integrating conventional lead-based oxide perovskites onto Si platforms remains challenging, owing to compositional complexity, chemical incompatibility, and thermal-budget constraints. Here, using first-principles calculations, we identify a strain-driven self-morphotropic phase boundary (SMPB) in lanthanum tungsten nitride (LaWN3, LWN). Biaxial strain (η) induces a sequential symmetry progression and enables polarization rotation and ultrahigh piezoelectric responses. We further demonstrate that this SMPB is dynamically tunable by an electric field, yielding ultrahigh piezoelectric stress (eij) and strain (dij) coefficients that exceed those of conventional nitride piezoelectrics (e.g., AlN, AlScN, GaScN) by orders of magnitude. Our results establish a deterministic pathway to ultrahigh piezoelectricity in nitride perovskites, offering a compelling materials platform for adaptive electromechanical devices in next-generation telecommunications and integrated microelectronics.
